7759: RV park on Highway 6 in the historic Victorian antique town of Calvert, in Robertson County, Central Texas, with spacious sites, restrooms and a pavilion; tents are welcome too, and stays can be nightly, weekly or monthly. --Claude
7771: Large 100-acre campground and event park by Grapeland in East Texas, built around a 2-acre spring-fed swimming lake, with hundreds of RV sites, most of them 30-amp, plus cabins.  It hosts several music festivals a year, bluegrass among them, and takes nightly RV campers too. --Claude
7803: Gated RV park around a private 30-acre lake in Vidor, near Beaumont in Southeast Texas, with lakefront and shaded sites, a bathhouse and catch-and-release fishing for guests; the lake also has a summer water park with a sandy beach. --Claude
7808: Small RV park on Bell Street on the south side of Amarillo, about 20 minutes from Palo Duro Canyon State Park, with a bathhouse; it takes monthly stays as well as nightly ones. --Claude
7823: Destination RV park in the Frio River canyon on US 83 at Concan, about 2.7 miles from Garner State Park, with oak-shaded sites, fire pits, patios and some covered spaces, cable TV, a pool, a playground, a community building, a fishing pond stocked with catfish, bass and perch, and rental cabins. --Claude
7832: 75-acre Hill Country resort by the Guadalupe River on River Road outside New Braunfels, with cabins, cottages, treetop villas, tipis, pioneer wagons and primitive tent sites besides the RV sites, pools and a hot tub, mini-golf, sports courts, a clubhouse and river tubing, for nightly and weekly stays. --Claude
7833: RV resort in Fulton, half a mile from downtown and about 3 miles from Rockport Beach, with a concrete driveway and patio on every site, cable TV, a pool and a covered picnic area; pop-up campers and tents aren't allowed, and stays can be nightly, weekly or monthly. --Claude
7849: RV park off I-10 in Vidor, in Southeast Texas's Golden Triangle, with concrete pads, satellite TV, a dog park and two catch-and-release fishing ponds, for overnight and long stays. --Claude
7851: Small RV park on West Highland Avenue (FM 1069) in Aransas Pass, with grassy, shaded sites, central to Rockport, Port Aransas and Corpus Christi for Coastal Bend fishing. --Claude
7857: Newer coastal RV park near Copano Bay on the Lamar peninsula outside Rockport, with extra-wide, deep concrete or gravel sites aimed at boaters and anglers, beside a 950-acre wildlife sanctuary, for nightly, weekly or monthly stays. --Claude
7859: Small gated RV park on FM 317 near Chandler, about 2 miles from Lake Palestine, with 35-by-65-foot sites and a dog park, for a night or by the week or month. --Claude
7868: Small RV park on FM 2978 near Magnolia, northwest of Houston, with two stocked fishing ponds, shady sites and cable TV, for nightly, weekly or monthly stays. --Claude
7873: RV park beside the Traders Village Houston weekend flea market off North Eldridge Road, with level concrete sites, restrooms, a pool, a rec hall and propane. --Claude
7878: RV park in Anahuac near Trinity Bay and Fort Anahuac Park, open since 1998, with a choice of shaded grass or concrete pads, landscaped grounds, a pool and cabins, for nightly or weekly stays. --Claude
7908: RV park on Highway 64 west of Tyler with big 50-by-125-foot sites, each with a concrete patio, a fire pit and a picnic table; the premium back-ins are fenced on both sides, and there are a pool, a hot tub and propane. --Claude
7923: Newer RV park at the junction of US 281 and US 84 in Evant, in Central Texas about an hour from Waco and Fort Cavazos, beside the WinStop gas station and store and the WinWash laundromat, with level sites. --Claude
7928: 116-acre piney-woods RV park and event venue on FM 1798 near Mount Enterprise, about 15 minutes south of Henderson in East Texas, with restrooms, rustic cabins, open-field tent camping, a clubhouse and walking trails; some sites have water and power but no sewer, and the park hosts concerts and motorcycle shows. --Claude
8047: Town of Bernalillo campground near the Rio Grande just off US 550, about 15 miles north of Albuquerque, next to the Coronado Historic Site and looking out on the Sandia Mountains, with restrooms and a tent area with sheltered sites that closes from November to March. --Claude
8061: Route 66 RV park on the east side of Tucumcari with gravel sites, 45 of them double-wide pull-throughs for big rigs, three restrooms with walk-in showers, a rec room open around the clock, a dog run and a few horse stalls; a handful of sites also take tents. --Claude
8079: Large RV park, formerly Circle B, on US 70 at Ruidoso Downs, with more than 120 spaces, paved roads and room for big rigs, about 2 miles from the racetrack and near the Lincoln National Forest; it also rents long-term sites by the month. --Claude
8157: RV park and campground in an apple orchard on the Continental Divide in historic Pinos Altos, at about 7,000 feet, 6 to 7 miles north of Silver City on NM 15, with tent sites, cabins and tiny-home parking, for a night, a week or a month; it has been running since 1986, now under new owners. --Claude
8299: Saugeen Valley Conservation Authority campground 4 km north of Paisley by the Saugeen River, with 102 sites with 30-amp power and 79 without, plus a separate horse-camping loop; it is open from late April to about Thanksgiving. --Claude
8338: Daiva RV Resorts campground near Meaford, about 2 km inland from Georgian Bay, with 29 overnight sites besides 46 seasonal ones, a heated pool, a playground, a few cabins and rental trailers, and access to the Tom Thomson Trail. --Claude
8581: City of Cranbrook RV campground a short walk from downtown, run under contract for the city, with Joseph Creek running through it, power at most sites and washrooms; it is open from April to about Thanksgiving, and back-to-back bookings aren't allowed. --Claude
